title: Case 02: The Last Rehearsal
subtitle: A theater closes after a final rehearsal. A cracked watch, a white rose, and a fire alarm disagree about when the crime really happened.
loop_reset_text: The stage lights flare white. Applause runs backward. The cracked watch ticks again. Only you and Asma remember what did not fit.

theater.name: Raven Theater
theater.description: The final rehearsal ended early. Someone left the stage, someone lied about the alarm, and one seat in the front row is still warm.

backstage.name: Backstage Corridor
backstage.description: Costumes, prop tables, and a service door that should have been locked.

office.name: Director's Office
office.description: Contracts, donor records, and a clock that runs two minutes fast.

alley.name: Stage Door Alley
alley.description: Rain, a fire-exit alarm box, and rose petals stuck to the drain.

mira.name: Mira Vale
mira.asma_open: Look at me. She is too calm for someone who says she found the body.
dialogue: I left the stage before the alarm. Anton was still rehearsing.
You asked me about the rose last time. It was not from me. Check the dressing rooms.
The rose was part of the final scene, but one was missing before rehearsal began.

contradiction.result: Mira did not plant the rose. The torn ticket places her in the lobby during the critical window, but she knew a prop rose was missing.

tells: Mira Vale answers quickly, but their eyes move toward the nearest exit.
This time Mira Vale reacts before you finish the question. They remember nothing, but the pattern changed.
Mira Vale tries to repeat the same wording. One detail is different.
mira.pressure_line: You should not know that part yet.
mira.shadow_reveal: Mira Vale changes route after the interview and briefly checks a place they never mentioned.

anton.name: Anton Reeve
anton.asma_open: Something about his timing bothers me. Listen to the exact words he uses.
dialogue: The fire alarm went off at 10:12. I started evacuation immediately.
Yes, the watch says 10:17. Watches break. Alarm logs do not.
The alarm panel was serviced that afternoon. Someone could have delayed the local bell without changing the central log.

contradiction.result: Anton concealed that the local alarm could be delayed. His statement is technically true but intentionally misleading.

tells: Anton Reeve answers quickly, but their eyes move toward the nearest exit.
This time Anton Reeve reacts before you finish the question. They remember nothing, but the pattern changed.
Anton Reeve tries to repeat the same wording. One detail is different.
anton.pressure_line: That is not what I said before.
anton.shadow_reveal: Anton Reeve changes route after the interview and briefly checks a place they never mentioned.

julian.name: Julian Cross
julian.asma_open: He keeps watching your hands, not mine. He knows we found something.
dialogue: I was backstage fixing the blood rig. I never touched the stage-door alarm.
Fine. I moved the pocket watch. It was part of the set and I thought it had been damaged during rehearsal.
I picked it up before I knew anyone was dead. It was already stopped.

contradiction.result: Julian moved the watch and contaminated the scene, but his timeline suggests it stopped before he found it.

tells: Julian Cross answers quickly, but their eyes move toward the nearest exit.
This time Julian Cross reacts before you finish the question. They remember nothing, but the pattern changed.
Julian Cross tries to repeat the same wording. One detail is different.
julian.pressure_line: That is not what I said before.
julian.shadow_reveal: Julian Cross changes route after the interview and briefly checks a place they never mentioned.

celeste.name: Celeste Ward
celeste.asma_open: She wants us to think this is about the theater. I think it is about what the victim knew.
dialogue: The victim threatened to ruin the production. That is all.
Those donor records are private. They have nothing to do with a rehearsal accident.
The victim found payments routed through a shell foundation. I was trying to buy time, not kill anyone.

contradiction.result: Celeste had a financial motive and tried to delay exposure, but the records do not place her at the alarm panel.

tells: Celeste Ward answers quickly, but their eyes move toward the nearest exit.
This time Celeste Ward reacts before you finish the question. They remember nothing, but the pattern changed.
Celeste Ward tries to repeat the same wording. One detail is different.
celeste.pressure_line: That is not what I said before.
celeste.shadow_reveal: Celeste Ward changes route after the interview and briefly checks a place they never mentioned.

amir.name: Amir Hale
amir.asma_open: He says the blackout was accidental. I do not believe accidents repeat this neatly.
dialogue: The lights cut because the old dimmer board tripped.
You noticed the same flicker in the last loop. That pattern is not random.
Someone programmed a five-second blackout cue into the rehearsal stack. I did not write it.

contradiction.result: The blackout was programmed, not accidental. Amir knew the system well enough to recognize it, but the cue was added under another login.

tells: Amir Hale answers quickly, but their eyes move toward the nearest exit.
This time Amir Hale reacts before you finish the question. They remember nothing, but the pattern changed.
Amir Hale tries to repeat the same wording. One detail is different.
amir.pressure_line: That is not what I said before.
amir.shadow_reveal: Amir Hale changes route after the interview and briefly checks a place they never mentioned.

watch.name: Cracked Pocket Watch
watch.description: Stopped at 10:17. The crack is fresh, but the mechanism failed before impact.

ticket.name: Torn Theater Ticket
ticket.description: Seat B14 was scanned at 10:11 and torn again at 10:16.

rose.name: Blood-Specked White Rose
rose.description: One prop rose is missing from the final scene. Petals match those in the alley drain.
rose.locked_hint: You remember petals near the stage door, but you did not think to compare them before.

alarm.name: Central Fire Alarm Log
alarm.description: Central system logged activation at 10:12, five minutes before the watch stopped.

service.name: Alarm Service Report
service.description: The local bell relay was replaced that afternoon and left in test-delay mode.
service.locked_hint: The alarm panel looked ordinary before. Now you remember the maintenance sticker.

cue.name: Hidden Lighting Cue
cue.description: A five-second blackout cue was inserted into the rehearsal stack under a borrowed login.
cue.locked_hint: The blackout pattern feels familiar. You need another loop to notice exactly why.

ledger.name: Donor Ledger Copy
ledger.description: Payments were routed through a shell foundation tied to the theater owner.

contract.name: Unsigned Cancellation Contract
contract.description: The victim planned to cancel the production and expose the shell foundation the next morning.
contract.locked_hint: A folded document on the desk seems unimportant the first time through.

keycard.name: Stage Door Keycard Log
keycard.description: A duplicate staff card opened the stage door at 10:10, then again at 10:18.
keycard.locked_hint: The door sensor chirp is easy to miss. By the third loop, you know exactly when to listen.

timeline: 10:07 PM — One prop rose is reported missing.
10:10 PM — Stage door opens with a duplicate staff card.
10:12 PM — Central fire alarm logs activation.
10:13 PM — Programmed blackout cue runs for five seconds.
10:16 PM — Torn ticket is scanned again.
10:18 PM — Stage door opens a second time.
deduction_prompt: Who manipulated the theater timeline, and what were they trying to hide?
truth: Anton used the maintenance delay on the local alarm and a programmed blackout cue to create a false timeline around the victim's death. He moved through the stage door with a duplicate card, then relied on the central alarm log to make the later time seem impossible. The deeper reason the loop keeps returning is still unresolved.
partial: You identify the false timeline but cannot prove who controlled both the alarm delay and stage-door access.
wrong: Your theory leaves the duplicated keycard, delayed alarm, and programmed blackout unexplained. The stage lights flare and the rehearsal starts again.

loop_reveals.2: You were right about the timing. This loop, do not chase the body first. Watch the alarm panel and the rose.
loop_reveals.3: I remember the stage-door chirp now. It happened before we ever looked at the alley. Someone is using the loop against the investigation.

action_beats.label: SEARCH THE SCENE WITH ASMA
action_beats.title: SCENE SEARCH
action_beats.text: Asma moves with you through the scene, checking what everyone else ignored. You compare positions, timing, and what looks slightly too deliberate.

action_beats.label: FOLLOW THE MOVEMENT YOU REMEMBER
action_beats.title: PURSUIT
action_beats.text: You move before the moment repeats. Asma follows your lead as you cut across the route you remember from the previous loop.

action_beats.label: TAKE COVER & HOLD POSITION
action_beats.title: TAKE COVER
action_beats.text: The situation turns dangerous. You and Asma take cover, wait for the opening, and move only when the evidence says the risk is worth it.

twist_hint: The obvious explanation for Case 02 is incomplete; one detail only makes sense after the loop repeats.
